title: Token Jumping in Planar Graphs has Linear Sized Kernels

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition of C_Y and later size sums in Claim 4/Claim 6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines C_Y := {v in V(G) : N(v) ∩ X = Y}, which includes the vertices of X themselves. However, later bounds use |V(G)| = |X| + |C_1| + |C_2| + |C_3| and |V(G')| ≤ |X| + |C_1| + |J_s ∪ J_t ∪ J_m| + |C_3|. Since X is already contained in the C_Y classes, adding |X| separately double-counts those vertices. Either the definition should exclude X, or the sums should omit |X|.

predicted_errors.error_location: Ordering of C_Y, paragraph after defining H_Y
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims: 'Further, since |f_0| ≥ 3 and y'y'' ∉ E(H_Y), in fact f_0 contains exactly two vertices in C_Y.' This is false when |C_Y| = 1, since then H_Y is the path y'-v-y'' and the outer face contains only one vertex of C_Y, not two. The assertion is therefore not valid as stated.

predicted_errors.error_location: After Claim 3: 'It is helpful to note ... G[C_Y] is a linear forest'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claim that G[C_Y] is a linear forest is false. For example, take X = {a,b} with I_s = {a}, I_t = {b} (k=1). Let C_Y = {c1,c2,c3}, with each c_i adjacent to both a and b, and add the triangle edges c1c2, c2c3, c3c1. The resulting graph is K5 minus the edge ab, which is planar, but G[C_Y] is a triangle, not a linear forest.

predicted_errors.error_location: Claim 7, base case of the induction
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The base case says: 'we move the token on y_1'' to z_1'.' But z_1' ∈ C_{Y_1} is adjacent to both y_1' and y_1''. Since y_1' still has a token at that point, placing a token on z_1' creates adjacent occupied vertices z_1' and y_1', violating the independent-set condition. The proof does not first move y_1', so this step is invalid.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph after J_s/J_t construction and in Claim 7
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says 'Since G[J_s ∪ J_t ∪ J_m] is a linear forest, by Claim 4 the answer to ISR-TJ(G', I_s, I_t) is YES' and later 'by Claim 4 we move all tokens...'. Claim 4 is the kernel-size bound when G_{P_Big} has no independent set of size k; the reconfiguration-in-linear-forest result is Claim 5. These cross-references are wrong.

predicted_errors.error_location: Construction of J_s and the proof of the |V(G')| ≤ 67k bound
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: If the construction of J_s stops early after finding an independent set of size k in ∪_{Y∈P^1} N^{Int}(Y), then it does not include the remaining vertices of C_Y for Y∈P^1. But G' is formed by deleting only (∪_{Y∈P_Big} N^{Int}(Y)) \ (J_m ∪ J_s ∪ J_t), so those uncollected P^1 vertices would remain in G'. The subsequent size bound assumes all remaining C_2 vertices are covered by J_s ∪ J_t ∪ J_m, so the early-stop case is not properly accounted for.
